title: Setting Up the Development Environment knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Setting Up the Development Environment”?
options: Setting Up the Development Environment means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Setting Up the Development Environment removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Setting Up the Development Environment should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Setting Up the Development Environment helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.answer_key: Setting Up the Development Environment helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Setting Up the Development Environment is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Installing a supported Node.js version” in this lesson?
options: Assume “Installing a supported Node.js version” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Installing a supported Node.js version” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Installing a supported Node.js version” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Installing a supported Node.js version” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Installing a supported Node.js version” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Installing a supported Node.js version” under Setting Up the Development Environment. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Setting Up the Development Environment”?
options: Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
